title: Secret or Cipher?
summary: Classify encoding, hashing, and encryption correctly.
description: Security terms are not interchangeable. Base64 is a reversible encoding, SHA-256 is a one-way hash function, and encryption is reversible when the correct key is available. Use harmless examples and create a JSON report with the correct classifications.

offline_hints.title: Think about the concept
offline_hints.content: Ask what security property each operation provides and whether a key is needed to reverse it.

offline_hints.title: Investigate this area
offline_hints.content: Review `examples.json`; a Base64 string can be decoded, a hash is not intended to be reversed, and encryption requires a key to decrypt.

offline_hints.title: Guided route
offline_hints.content: Create `crypto-report.json` with `base64: encoding`, `sha256: hashing`, `fernet: encryption`, and `hash_is_reversible: false`.

completion_explanation: Encoding changes representation but does not hide information from someone who can decode it. Hashing maps data to a digest and is not a reversible encryption scheme. Encryption is designed to be reversed by an authorised holder of the decryption key.

network_requirements.description: No network interface is required for this mission.
